author: Moksh Trehan
capture_note: All photographs in this report were supplied by the author for this assignment. Three overlapping sets depict a basketball court, an indoor lounge, and a city view; two additional photographs show book covers for rectification. The intended mosaic model is camera rotation about a fixed center. Camera motion was not measured, and depth-dependent residuals are consistent with foreground parallax and departures from that model.

scene1.capture: Three central frames of the basketball-court sweep (IMG_1242–1244) share the window wall and backboard. IMG_1243 is the reference.
scene1.manual: Twelve manually observed window-frame landmarks constrain each adjacent pair. After manual alignment, automatic image-content seams and multiband blending keep the hoop intact. The feather-only baselines remain available for comparison.
scene1.comparison: Both results use the same automatic seam algorithm and multiband settings. The backboard, rim, and net remain intact without any hand-selected source region. Their sharpness demonstrates improved compositing; the lower-window crop shows that local geometric disagreements still remain.
scene1.limitations: The backboard, net, window structure, and distant exterior lie at different depths. A single homography cannot align all of them if the camera translates. Automatic source selection reduces duplicated edges but does not correct parallax; a seam can still cross another object.
scene1.refinement_caption: Identical automatic homographies before and after compositing. Left: feathering averages displaced edges. Right: a seam chosen from image disagreement and edge strength avoids the hoop, retaining a coherent backboard, rim, and net. All content comes from the supplied photographs.
refinement_note: The initial feathered mosaic doubled the backboard and rim because the foreground object occupies different locations across the views. The automatic seam refinement keeps it intact while retaining the estimated homographies.

No hoop detector or manually specified rectangle is used. The same algorithm and parameters are applied to manual and automatic geometry in both indoor scenes. The coverage masks are verified to equal those of the feather baselines. This changes source selection, not the geometric estimate.
scene1.detail_caption: Manual alignment (left) and automatic alignment (right), both with automatic seams: lower-window detail cropped at identical reference coordinates.
scene1.compositor: automatic seam selection with multiband blending
scene1.refinement_title: An intact hoop from automatic seams

scene2.capture: Four overlapping lounge views, ordered IMG_1247, IMG_1248, IMG_1250, IMG_1249. IMG_1248 is the reference; the last two images are ordered by scene overlap rather than filename.
scene2.manual: Nine, ten, and ten visually selected landmarks constrain the adjacent pairs. Reviewing the original photographs resolved ambiguous frame corners and wall junctions, lowering fitting RMS errors from 3.04/3.21/2.83 to 1.46/0.95/1.04 working pixels. Automatic seams then preserve clearer masonry, artwork, and chandelier detail. These are fit residuals, not independent accuracy measurements.
scene2.comparison: Both results now use the same automatic seam and multiband compositor. Refined manual landmarks produce a clearer fireplace wall than the initial manual fit, while the automatic result also maintains coherent stone courses and artwork edges. Narrow detail transitions avoid broad duplicated chandelier arms and bulbs.
scene2.limitations: The furniture, chandelier, corridor, and fireplace wall occupy different depths. Source selection reduces their visible doubling, but it cannot make a single homography explain all viewpoints. Local discontinuities and exposure transitions can remain, particularly near furniture and the ceiling.
scene2.compositor: automatic seam selection with multiband blending

scene3.capture: Three overlapping outdoor views (IMG_1251–1253), with IMG_1252 as the reference. Buildings provide static landmarks distributed across the lower half of the images; the sky is not used for manual annotations.
scene3.manual: Ten and eleven visually selected landmarks constrain the two adjacent pairs. Refining ambiguous roof tips and using clear roof corners reduced the fitting residuals; the rooflines and chimney now remain sharp across most overlaps.
scene3.comparison: Both methods recover a coherent panorama from the same three photographs. The manual fits use 10 and 11 carefully observed landmarks, while the automatic fits retain 137/153 and 108/127 descriptor matches. These are fitting statistics, not independent accuracy measurements.
scene3.limitations: Most landmarks are below the horizon, so the upper sky and outer image boundaries are extrapolated. Thin roof edges remain sensitive to small point-placement errors; the clouds are not assumed to be fixed geometric landmarks.

descriptor_caption: One actual matched feature from each reference image. Left: the original 40 × 40 grayscale neighborhood. Middle: the same neighborhood after Gaussian blur (σ = 2). Right: eight samples per axis, five pixels apart, normalized to zero mean and unit standard deviation. Normalized displays share the range −2 to +2; the exact 64 values are saved with the figure data.

validation.summary: Checks cover homography recovery and degeneracy, inverse sampling and valid black pixels, ANMS and descriptors, ratio matching, RANSAC with outliers, transform chains, and project configuration. Ten seam-specific tests include an exhaustive minimum-path comparison, a shifted-object case, source validity, coverage, constant-field reconstruction, and band blending. Earlier compositor tests remain as regression checks.

blend_caption: Lounge with identical automatic homographies: feather baseline (left), automatic seams and multiband blending (right). The chandelier and masonry are clearer. Source coverage is unchanged; local seams and parallax can still remain. Sequential vertical seams assume a predominantly horizontal panorama.
corner_display_caption: Tiny translucent markers preserve the photograph beneath every candidate; the lower row enlarges the same cyan-box region in both columns. No points are subsampled.
blend_method: The indoor scenes additionally use an automatic compositor after geometric estimation. Registered views are ordered by their projected horizontal centers. For each incoming view, a custom dynamic program chooses a top-to-bottom seam through the overlap. It favors similar colors and avoids strong edges, so large misaligned objects are less likely to be cut or averaged.

The seam cost uses RGB absolute disagreement smoothed at σ = 3 pixels, plus 0.6 times smoothed gradient strength and a 0.012 overlap-centering penalty. It is evaluated every four pixels; each step may move up to three sampled columns. A 2-pixel Gaussian transition forms the intermediate composite used to compare the next view.

Final blending decomposes each source into full-resolution Gaussian/residual bands at σ = 3, 12, and 48 pixels. Ownership masks use σ = 1, 3, 12, and 48 pixels from finest to coarsest band. Weights are normalized over valid sources. Fine detail changes narrowly at the seam; wider low-frequency transitions soften exposure differences. The same settings are used for both indoor scenes and both alignment methods.
